title: Phantom Shadow Traffic Curve Manager: configurable canary schedules and rollback thresholds
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary:
Introduce the 'Phantom' manager: a policy and configuration layer that 1) shapes shadow traffic along a configurable traffic curve (not just fixed percentages), 2) ties A/B and canary steps to composite signal windows, and 3) defines automated, graded rollback behaviors based on signal divergence and user-visible error budgets. This ticket implements the policy engine and a runtime-facing config DSL; a follow-up will add UI for Console.

Background:
Current canary tooling supports stepping traffic percentages and simple metric gates. We frequently see workloads where a shadow-only probing phase and a smoothed ramp (nonlinear traffic curve) reduce noise and provide better signal for quality regressions. Also, teams want automatic soft-rollbacks (throttle back) before full rollback to avoid noisy aborts.

Goals:
- Provide a compact DSL to define shadow curves, step schedules, and multi-signal guardrails.
- Implement runtime enforcers for traffic shaping and automated throttling/rollback actions.
- Emit telemetry and event hooks for Console to visualize phase, risk score, and automated actions.

Non-goals:
- Full Console integration (separate UX ticket).
- Model-level offline evaluation pipelines (this is runtime-only rollout tooling).

Requirements (MUST):
- Support shadow phase: configurable duration where traffic is mirrored to candidate without affecting production routing; percent of requests fed to shadow can follow a curve (time->percent).
- Support canary phases that accept a schedule of (t0: p0 -> t1: p1 ...), where p is effective fraction of production requests. Curves allowed: linear, exponential decay/growth, custom piecewise.
- Composite gates: allow metric expressions combining latency, 5xx-rate, token-per-request regression, and custom evals (e.g., semantic-eval divergence).
- Automated actions: NOOP, THROTTLE (reduce curve slope), PAUSE (hold at current percent), ROLLBACK (traffic->baseline).
- Graceful rollback windows and soft-corrections (e.g., try reducing by 50% for 10m before full rollback).

Design notes:
- Policy engine is declarative and evaluated in the control plane; runtime agents receive compact directives (phase, target percentage, action) every evaluation tick (default 30s).
- Shadow traffic is routed via mirrored requests with isolated KV caches and trace tags for correlation; the manager can optionally enable non-critical out-of-band evals (semantic scoring) that do not add user-visible latency.
- Risk scoring: compute a rolling z-score per metric against baseline window; combine via weighted sum to derive a single risk score 0..100. Thresholds in policy map to actions.
- Soft rollback strategy: when risk in [throttle_threshold, pause_threshold), emit THROTTLE action and reduce slope by throttle_factor for throttle_duration; when >= pause_threshold but < rollback_threshold, PAUSE; when >= rollback_threshold, ROLLBACK.

Config DSL example (YAML-like, stored in model rollout config):

phases:
  - name: "shadow-probe"
    mode: "shadow"
    duration: "30m"
    curve: "custom"
    curve_points: ["0m:0%","5m:5%","15m:20%","30m:50%"]
    metrics: ["latency_p95","errors_5xx","semantic_divergence"]
  - name: "canary-1"
    mode: "canary"
    schedule:
      type: "exponential"
      start_percent: 1
      target_percent: 20
      duration: "2h"
    gates:
      - metric: "errors_5xx"
        op: ">="
        value: 0.02
        severity: "high"
      - metric: "semantic_divergence"
        op: ">="
        value: 0.12
        severity: "medium"
    soft_rollback:
      throttle_threshold: 40
      pause_threshold: 70
      rollback_threshold: 90
      throttle_factor: 0.5
      throttle_duration: "10m"

Actions and operator semantics are encoded in the policy compiler to produce compact runtime directives.

Telemetry and alerts:
- Emit phase transitions (phase.enter, phase.exit) with vector: {model, route, phase, directive}.
- Risk score time-series and per-metric z-scores.
- Automated action events (throttle_applied, pause_applied, rolled_back) include windowed metrics and snapshot of active traffic curve.
- Console dashboard should allow replaying the curve and seeing which action triggered.

API / Runtime contract:
- Control plane exposes POST /rollouts/:id/compile -> compiled policy blob (opaque JSON string) + checksum.
- Edge agent polls GET /policy/:checksum -> directive {phase, effective_percent, action, next_eval_after}. (Implementation detail: compact protocol buffer on wire).

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit + integration tests for policy compiler with at least 10 policy permutations (shadow-only, soft-rollback only, piecewise curves).
- End-to-end test exercising simulated metrics that trigger soft-throttle and full rollback.
- Runtime agent receives directives and adjusts local traffic routing appropriately (shadow mirror enabled, traffic percentage applied).
- Console event stream shows phase events and automated actions (smoke verification).

Testing plan:
- Local simulated runtime harness (python load generator + mock metrics) to validate risk scoring and actions. PR will include a test suite runnable in CI.
- Chaos test: inject flapping 5xx in canary and verify throttle then pause then rollback progression.

Security / Compliance:
- No PII in mirrored shadow requests by default; mirror redactters applied unless explicit customer opt-in.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Complexity of curve semantics may confuse users; mitigate by shipping templates (linear-slow, bursty-probe, conservative-anchor).
- Shadow processing cost — default shadow percent capped at 50% and must be billable flag for hosted accounts.
- Telemetry noise: use robust baselining (rolling windows with outlier trimming).

Next steps / rollout plan:
1) Merge policy compiler and runtime agent support behind feature-flag (runtime-1.22). (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4278)
2) Add E2E tests and feature-flag in Canary testbed.
3) Console work item to display controls and allow live override.
